turns.assessment: The outage is node-wide around S15: all interrupted or protection-switched services depend on S15, including svc300, while services use many different optical degrees and channels. A single client, line-interface, span, amplifier, or WSS input-port fault cannot explain that breadth. The unchanged optical power/OSNR and coherent quality measurements strongly favor an ODU-layer failure rather than loss or degradation of the optical plant, making the S15 OTN switch fabric the common cause.

proposals.rationale: A switch-fabric failure at S15 interrupts every ODU cross-connected there, matching the simultaneous loss of many unrelated services whose common dependency is S15. It also explains why protected services moved to protection while optical telemetry showed no corresponding physical-layer change.
proposals.note: site named; resolved to its node equipment

proposals.rationale: A hard WSS failure at roadm.S15 could produce optical LOS, but the affected services arrive over multiple degrees, whereas the documented mode affects only one WSS input port. The unchanged optical telemetry also weighs strongly against it.
A line-card failure could interrupt one channel, but cannot account for the many independent S15 lightpaths and services affected simultaneously.
